questions.answer: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) is a strategic framework for making sure your brand appears in AI-generated search results and recommendations. It involves optimizing your digital footprint so AI systems recognize your brand as authoritative, relevant, and trustworthy, which covers content strategy, entity optimization, reputation signals, and technical implementation [6]. Joe describes GEO as broader and longer term than AEO, focused on making a brand a recognized entity that AI systems mention by name [5].

questions.answer: The 40-word rule is Joe's approach to structuring paragraphs so AI systems can cite them. He uses it to keep answer paragraphs short and self-contained, usually opening each page with a direct answer and question-style headings [4]. On this site, the rule is also described as the 40-word paragraph rule that lets AI systems extract content cleanly [5]. For more detail, see [The 40-Word Rule](/blog/the-40-word-rule-how-to-structure-paragraphs-for-ai-citations-in-2026/).

questions.q: How should I write paragraphs so AI tools quote them?
failed: Uses only links found in the sources
questions.answer: The site's guidance is to open each section with a question-style H2 or H3 heading, then write a definition block of 40 to 60 words that answers it directly, starting with the subject and a verb and avoiding preamble [2]. Expand with supporting evidence, examples, or data afterward, since that part can be longer than the answer block [2]. The site also notes that expert-attributed statistics help content get cited in AI retrieval [2]. If you want help applying this to your own site, you can reach Joe through the [contact page](/contact/).
